_doc: Redacted wg-quick profiles for the Cloud SuperApp full-config artifact, ONE MAP PER PEER (profiles.<peer id>.<profile id>). SECURITY: the PrivateKey VALUE is stripped at the source boundary, so this PUBLIC repo can never carry it. Real keys stay in cloud-vault (PRIVATE); the device holds its own key and imports it from file.
_source: cloud-vault/A0_keys/providers/wireguard/<peer.vault_wg_dir>/config-* for every peer in superapp-users.json that declares vault_wg_dir

v4-full.name: wg-v4-full
v4-full.config_text:
# wg-v4-full — IPv4 wifi, FULL tunnel (v4 via gcp-proxy, v6 via oci-analytics)
# Identity: termux (10.0.0.9 + fd0c:1d00::9 wg0 / 10.1.0.9 + fd0c:1d01::9 wg-public)
# DNS is MESH-ONLY (hickory 10.0.0.1 via gcp-proxy, unbound-DNS64 10.1.0.1 /
# fd0c:1d01::1 via oci-analytics) — two resolvers over two hubs = in-mesh
# redundancy, no external resolver ever.

[Interface]
PrivateKey = <PROVIDED_BY_DEVICE>
Address = 10.0.0.9/24, 10.1.0.9/24, fd0c:1d00::9/64, fd0c:1d01::9/64
MTU = 1380
DNS = 10.0.0.1, 10.1.0.1

[Peer]
# gcp-proxy — all IPv4 internet (gcp-proxy has no v6 egress) + wg0 mesh v6.
# fd0c:1d00::/64 MUST be listed here even though v6 egress goes to
# oci-analytics: it is more specific than the other peer's ::/0, so mesh v6
# reaches the hub directly instead of being handed to oci-analytics (which
# drops it — termux's allowed source there is fd0c:1d01::9, not fd0c:1d00::9).
PublicKey = vV/phXUwnCjxACQ5Df11Uw47BzJaK4r85jPYMu2HmDc=
Endpoint = 35.226.147.64:443
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, fd0c:1d00::/64
PersistentKeepalive = 25

[Peer]
# oci-analytics — wg-public mesh + ALL IPv6 (it has v6 egress + NAT64)
PublicKey = Bnyf83VpvGY4BjcjQEXgutNEzx9OXMltHIcKNh7cKkc=
Endpoint = 129.151.228.66:51821
AllowedIPs = 10.1.0.0/24, fd0c:1d01::/64, ::/0
PersistentKeepalive = 25

v6-full.name: wg-v6-full
v6-full.config_text:
# wg-v6-full — IPv6-only wifi, FULL tunnel for IPv4 (everything v4 via oci-analytics)
# NOT ::/0. A v6 default route covers this peer's own v6 endpoint, so the
# handshake packet is routed into the tunnel it is trying to establish and the
# peer never comes up (#523: last handshake 457s old under keepalive=25 — a
# total outage, worse than no VPN). Controlled A/B: same key, same endpoint,
# v6-split handshakes 5/5 and differs ONLY in AllowedIPs.
# Nothing is lost: on a v6-only uplink native-v6 sites are directly reachable,
# and IPv4-only hosts (github.com has no AAAA) ride 0.0.0.0/0 through the
# tunnel, which itself travels over IPv6 to the hub.
# Identity: termux (10.0.0.9 + fd0c:1d00::9 wg0 / 10.1.0.9 + fd0c:1d01::9 wg-public)
# DNS is MESH-ONLY (hickory 10.0.0.1 via gcp-proxy, unbound-DNS64 10.1.0.1 /
# fd0c:1d01::1 via oci-analytics) — two resolvers over two hubs = in-mesh
# redundancy, no external resolver ever.

# Address ORDER is load-bearing (#522): Android installs VPN routes with no
# preferred source, so the kernel sources EVERY IPv4 packet from the tun's
# FIRST IPv4 address. With 10.0.0.9 first, packets to 10.1.0.1 (and, in
# v6-full, all of 0.0.0.0/0) left as 10.0.0.9 and the wg-public hub dropped
# them as "unallowed src IP" (it allows 10.1.0.9/32 only) — 10.1.0.1 0/5
# while fd0c:1d01::1 was 5/5 (IPv6 picks its source by longest prefix, so
# it was never affected). oci-analytics is the only hub reachable on a
# v6-only uplink, so its address goes first; wg0 v4 (10.0.0.0/24) can only
# originate from here on dual-stack, which v4-* profiles are for.

[Interface]
PrivateKey = <PROVIDED_BY_DEVICE>
Address = 10.1.0.9/24, 10.0.0.9/24, fd0c:1d01::9/64, fd0c:1d00::9/64
MTU = 1380
DNS = fd0c:1d01::1, 10.1.0.1

[Peer]
# gcp-proxy — mesh reach when dual-stack; dead on v6-only wifi (harmless)
PublicKey = vV/phXUwnCjxACQ5Df11Uw47BzJaK4r85jPYMu2HmDc=
Endpoint = 35.226.147.64:443
AllowedIPs = 10.0.0.0/24, fd0c:1d00::/64
PersistentKeepalive = 25

[Peer]
# oci-analytics — ALL IPv4 traffic; DNS64/NAT64 reaches IPv4-only sites over v6.
# The v6 side is deliberately three specific prefixes, never ::/0: mesh
# (fd0c:1d01::/64, which is also the DNS64 resolver fd0c:1d01::1) and the
# NAT64 prefix the resolver synthesises into. Oracle's NAT64 prefix here is
# CUSTOM, not the well-known 64:ff9b::/96.
PublicKey = Bnyf83VpvGY4BjcjQEXgutNEzx9OXMltHIcKNh7cKkc=
Endpoint = [2603:c026:c104:8f00:0:c704:63b:6eee]:51821
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, fd0c:1d01::/64, 2603:c026:c104:8f00:ff9b::/96
PersistentKeepalive = 25
